messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: deprecating functions
parts:
Marco wrote:
> Are there other functions that already deprecated?
> I ask because I want to now the procedure here. I would suggest
> removing the deprecated functions from the manual and
> showing the user an error message asking to use the new function
> and refusing to continue compilation.

The Wikipedia has a nice description of deprecation:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deprecation

What we want to do is maintain backward compatibility by
not disturbing the behavior of existing programs. Then,
we print warning messages which include instructions on how
to recode so as to avoid the deprecation warnings.

At some release in the future where we break backward
compatibility, we remove the function altogether. We can
still print warnings, but don't need to at this point.

The idea is that if someone's program compiles without
deprecation warnings, it should work in future releases.

To implement deprecation, we are going to need to create
a set of deprecated function names then match them during
parsing to print a warning message that indicates how to fix
the code so the deprecation warning goes away.

- Bob

It probably makes sense to leave the deprecated functions
in the manual so that users can see the instructions on how
to remove them.

Also, adding a marker to the index would be nice. Shouldn't
be hard to write another macro in LaTeX or use the existing one
with some conventional markup.

I'm not even sure we need to deprecate anything yet.
Though it looks like we will be looking at lp__ soon.
